title: 2 Secrets Hidden Inside the Lamborghini Revuelto

scenes.text: The Lamborghini Revuelto has one thousand and one horsepower, a V12 that revs past nine thousand r p m, and a price tag that can pass eight hundred thousand dollars with options. But the two most interesting things about this car are hidden where most people never look. One of them is sideways. The other one runs right between your seats.
scenes.caption: 2 SECRETS INSIDE THE REVUELTO

scenes.text: In this video we open up the Revuelto and show you two secrets that explain the whole car. Why Lamborghini turned its gearbox ninety degrees, and why the battery of a one-thousand-horsepower supercar is smaller than the battery of many small hybrids. And the second secret changes how the car behaves every time you start it.
scenes.caption: SIDEWAYS AND BETWEEN THE SEATS

scenes.text: Along the way, you will see the bull it was named after, the door recall that could trap people inside, the new SV version that broke a lap record in twenty twenty-six, and what this car is really worth after six thousand miles. Every number comes from a published source, listed in the description.
scenes.caption: EVERY NUMBER IS SOURCED

scenes.text: First, a twist. The Revuelto is Lamborghini's first true hybrid. And the brand that built its legend on loud, wild V12s used electricity to make that V12 even more extreme, not more quiet.
scenes.caption: A HYBRID THAT IS NOT QUIET

scenes.text: Lamborghini names many of its cars after fighting bulls, and the Revuelto is no exception. According to Wikipedia, Revuelto was a Spanish fighting bull that fought in the Barcelona arena in the eighteen eighties. The car was unveiled online on the twenty-ninth of March twenty twenty-three, as the successor to the Aventador, and the design team was led by Mitja Borkert.
scenes.caption: NAMED AFTER A FIGHTING BULL

scenes.text: The Aventador it replaced was a big success. It was built from twenty eleven to twenty twenty-two, and reports at the end of its run put production at about eleven thousand four hundred sixty-five cars. It used a single-clutch automated gearbox for more than a decade, which many owners and reviewers found harsh. Lamborghini needed the next V12 to be a big leap.
scenes.caption: THE AVENTADOR: 2011 TO 2022

scenes.text: The Revuelto's numbers are enormous. The six point five liter naturally aspirated V12 makes about eight hundred fourteen horsepower at nine thousand two hundred fifty r p m. Three electric motors add more, for a total of one thousand and one horsepower. Zero to one hundred kilometers per hour takes two point five seconds, and top speed is about three hundred fifty kilometers per hour, or two hundred seventeen miles per hour.
scenes.caption: 1,001 HP

scenes.text: And the V12 itself is new. Car and Driver, via Yahoo Autos, reported a new block, valvetrain, and pistons, and said the engine is thirty-seven pounds lighter than the Aventador's V12. The redline is nine thousand five hundred r p m. But the most important changes are not in the engine. They are around it.
scenes.caption: 37 POUNDS LIGHTER

scenes.text: To understand why these secrets matter, you need to know how much the V12 means to Lamborghini. Ferruccio Lamborghini was already a successful industrialist who made tractors, boilers, and air conditioners when he founded Automobili Lamborghini in nineteen sixty-three to compete with Ferrari. His very first series car, the three fifty G T, used a V12 designed by Giotto Bizzarrini.
scenes.caption: 1963: A TRACTOR MAKER'S V12

scenes.text: Then came the Miura in nineteen sixty-six, with its V12 mounted behind the driver, a layout that defined the supercar. Then the Countach, whose name, according to Wikipedia, is a Piedmontese expletive, breaking the bull-name tradition. Then the Diablo and the Murcielago, both named after bulls. And then the Aventador. Every flagship Lamborghini has had a V12.
scenes.caption: MIURA, COUNTACH, DIABLO

scenes.text: The company itself survived chaos. Wikipedia lists a bankruptcy in nineteen seventy-eight, a period in receivership, ownership by Chrysler from nineteen eighty-seven to nineteen ninety-four, then Indonesian investors, and finally Audi, part of the Volkswagen Group, from nineteen ninety-eight. Through all of it, the V12 flagship survived.
scenes.caption: OWNERS CHANGED, THE V12 STAYED

scenes.text: So when emissions rules made a pure V12 harder to sell, Lamborghini faced a real choice. Drop the V12, like many brands moved to smaller turbo engines, or find a way to keep it. The Revuelto is the answer, and the two secrets in this video are how Lamborghini made that answer work.
scenes.caption: DROP THE V12, OR SAVE IT?

scenes.text: Secret number one. The Revuelto's gearbox is sideways. In the Aventador, the gearbox sat in front of the engine, in the middle of the car. In the Revuelto, the new eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox sits behind the engine, mounted transversely, across the car, at ninety degrees to the direction you drive.
scenes.caption: SECRET 1: THE GEARBOX IS SIDEWAYS

scenes.text: Why would anyone do that? According to the reporting, Lamborghini chose the transverse layout to optimize the center of gravity and to free up space underneath the rear of the car for a working diffuser. A diffuser is the shaped floor at the back that helps suck the car to the road. With the gearbox out of the way, the air can flow better.
scenes.caption: ROOM FOR A REAL DIFFUSER

scenes.text: And there is a second reason, which is the twist. Moving the gearbox out of the middle of the car left an empty space in the central tunnel, between the driver and passenger. That empty space is where Lamborghini put something else entirely. And that brings us to secret number two.
scenes.caption: AN EMPTY TUNNEL

scenes.text: But before that, notice what the gearbox does for the driver. The Aventador used a single-clutch robotized gearbox with seven speeds. The Revuelto moves to eight speeds and two clutches. Motor1 noted that this replaced the Aventador's seven-speed robotized unit. In everyday driving, that is one of the biggest differences an owner feels.
scenes.caption: FROM 1 CLUTCH TO 2

scenes.text: On top of that sideways gearbox sits one of the electric motors. It can connect to or disconnect from the V12 depending on the drive mode. It can help with power, and in low-grip conditions it can use extra energy from the V12 to recharge the battery. So the gearbox is not just sideways. It is also a power station.
scenes.caption: A MOTOR ON TOP OF THE GEARBOX

scenes.text: The front of the car has two more electric motors, one per wheel. Each makes up to about one hundred forty-seven horsepower, according to the report, and because they are separate, the car can send different amounts of power to each front wheel. That is called torque vectoring. It helps the car turn into corners like a smaller car.
scenes.caption: ONE MOTOR PER FRONT WHEEL

scenes.text: Secret number two. The battery is the spine of the car. The Revuelto's three point eight kilowatt hour battery runs lengthwise through the central tunnel, where the gearbox used to be. Car and Driver described it as acting like a spine inside the carbon fiber monocoque, between the driver and the passenger.
scenes.caption: SECRET 2: THE BATTERY IS A SPINE

scenes.text: And here is the surprise. Three point eight kilowatt hours is tiny. Many plug-in hybrid family cars have batteries several times bigger. Wikipedia lists the Revuelto's electric-only range at about ten kilometers, or six miles, on the European test. So the battery is not there to make the car an electric car. It is there to make the V12 car faster.
scenes.caption: ONLY 6 MILES ON ELECTRIC

scenes.text: That small battery can be refilled very quickly. According to the report, it recharges from a plug in about thirty minutes, and it can go from empty to full in about six minutes using the V12 or the brakes. In other words, the car is constantly filling and emptying that battery as you drive, using it like a power booster.
scenes.caption: EMPTY TO FULL IN 6 MINUTES

scenes.text: The battery position matters for weight balance too. It sits low and in the center of the car, which is the best place for heavy parts. And it helps the carbon fiber monocoque, which Car and Driver reported is ten percent lighter and twenty-five percent stiffer than the Aventador's, even though it is bigger to fit taller drivers.
scenes.caption: 10% LIGHTER, 25% STIFFER

scenes.text: So here is the twist about the battery. Lamborghini used the smallest possible electric part to change the biggest number. Total power rose to one thousand and one horsepower, the front wheels got their own motors, and the car got an electric mode. But the V12 still does most of the work.
scenes.caption: SMALL BATTERY, BIG EFFECT

scenes.text: And yes, the car has an electric mode. It is called Citta, which is Italian for city. It reduces power and lets the car drive on electricity for short distances. But Top Gear, in its twenty twenty-five Performance Car of the Year, said the Revuelto is still loud and dramatic, even in electric mode. A Lamborghini that tries to whisper, and cannot.
scenes.caption: CITTA MODE: STILL LOUD

scenes.text: So do these secrets work? According to Lamborghini, as reported by Car and Driver, the Revuelto is quicker than the Aventador S V J both on track and in a straight line. The S V J was the most extreme Aventador. The car that replaced it is faster than its wildest version.
scenes.caption: FASTER THAN THE SVJ

scenes.text: Aerodynamics improved too. The same report said the Revuelto is sixty percent more aerodynamically efficient and makes seventy percent more downforce than the Aventador. Wikipedia describes an active rear spoiler, and an active aero system Lamborghini calls A L A. That working diffuser, made possible by the sideways gearbox, is part of that story.
scenes.caption: 70% MORE DOWNFORCE

scenes.text: Then came the verdict that matters to enthusiasts. In Top Gear's Performance Car of the Year for twenty twenty-five, the Revuelto faced the Ferrari twelve Cilindri and the Aston Martin Vanquish. Top Gear called the Revuelto its winner on track, and said its chassis can keep pace with its engine.
scenes.caption: TOP GEAR'S TRACK WINNER

scenes.text: Top Gear also said it has genuine depth and nuance, and called it a supercar that wants to have fun and knows how to play. Coming from a test that included a Ferrari V12, that is high praise. And part of the reason is the front electric motors and the balance from the battery spine.
scenes.caption: IT WANTS TO HAVE FUN

scenes.text: The brakes are huge too. Wikipedia lists carbon-ceramic discs of four hundred ten millimeters at the front with ten-piston calipers, and three hundred ninety millimeters at the rear. Stopping one thousand eight hundred eighty kilograms from more than three hundred kilometers per hour takes serious hardware.
scenes.caption: 10-PISTON CALIPERS

scenes.text: The acceleration numbers show how the hybrid system works together. Wikipedia lists zero to one hundred kilometers per hour in two point five seconds, zero to two hundred in six point six seconds, and zero to three hundred in fifteen point three seconds. The electric motors fill the gaps at low speed, and the V12 pulls hard all the way to nine thousand r p m.
scenes.caption: 0-300 KM/H IN 15.3 S

scenes.text: And this is not a small car. It is about four point nine five meters long and more than two meters wide, with a curb weight of about one thousand eight hundred eighty kilograms according to Wikipedia. That is heavier than the Aventador it replaced, because of the motors and the battery. The two secrets are how Lamborghini made a heavier car feel lighter.
scenes.caption: HEAVIER, BUT IT FEELS LIGHTER

scenes.text: And Lamborghini was not done. In August twenty twenty-six, at Monterey Car Week in California, it revealed the Revuelto S V. Auto123 reported a total output of about one thousand fifty-one horsepower, a new front splitter, a redesigned underbody, and a double rear wing. Downforce rose by about eighty percent over the regular Revuelto.
scenes.caption: THE REVUELTO SV

scenes.text: The S V lapped the Hockenheimring in one minute forty-one point six seconds with factory driver Marco Mapelli, which Auto123 described as the fastest time recorded there by a production car. Zero to one hundred takes two point four seconds. And production is limited to one thousand nine hundred sixty-three cars, a nod to the year Lamborghini was founded.
scenes.caption: 1:41.6 AT HOCKENHEIM

scenes.text: Here is the twist. Motor1 reported a United States order sheet price of seven hundred forty-one thousand one hundred seventy-two dollars before options for the S V, and said most allocations go to existing customers and collectors. So for most people, the question is not whether they can afford it, but whether Lamborghini will let them buy it.
scenes.caption: $741,172 BEFORE OPTIONS

scenes.text: No car is perfect, and the Revuelto had a recall that sounds like a movie scene. In July twenty twenty-five, AutoGuide reported a recall for twenty-seven United States Revuelto cars from the twenty twenty-four and twenty twenty-five model years. The problem was in the famous scissor doors.
scenes.caption: A DOOR RECALL

scenes.text: Some spherical support pins on the gas springs that hold the doors up had been installed incorrectly. If a pin came loose, the door could drop suddenly with a lot of force. A failure could also make the door hard to open from the inside, which could trap the occupants. Lamborghini said there was no warning sign of the issue.
scenes.caption: DOORS COULD DROP

scenes.text: The fix was simple. Dealers inspected the pins and replaced them if needed, for free, and owners were notified by mail starting in September. Only twenty-seven cars were involved. But it is a reminder that the most iconic feature of a Lamborghini, the doors that open upward, is also one of the most complicated.
scenes.caption: THE ICON IS COMPLICATED

scenes.text: Now demand. In July twenty twenty-three, months before the first deliveries, Motor Authority reported that the Revuelto was already sold out for about two years. At the time, the starting price outside the United States was about five hundred thousand euros. And the car was still largely hand-built, by around five hundred people.
scenes.caption: SOLD OUT FOR 2 YEARS

scenes.text: Wikipedia lists production of one thousand four hundred six Revueltos in twenty twenty-four. That year, duPont Registry reported that Lamborghini delivered a record ten thousand six hundred eighty-seven cars worldwide, more than six percent above twenty twenty-three, and said the Revuelto led the charge.
scenes.caption: 1,406 BUILT IN 2024

scenes.text: Here is the twist on value. In October twenty twenty-six, autoevolution looked at a twenty twenty-four Revuelto with about six thousand miles, offered for six hundred twenty-nine thousand nine hundred eighty dollars. It said used Revueltos start around six hundred thousand dollars and can reach almost nine hundred thousand, depending on options and condition.
scenes.caption: USED: $600K TO $900K

scenes.text: And the new price kept rising. Kelley Blue Book lists a starting sticker of about six hundred seventy-three thousand dollars for the twenty twenty-six Revuelto. Jalopnik's October twenty twenty-six test car had a base price of six hundred sixty-four thousand seven hundred ninety-nine dollars and came to eight hundred six thousand five hundred twenty-one with options, destination, and gas guzzler tax.
scenes.caption: $806,521 AS TESTED

scenes.text: In that test car, two carbon fiber packages alone cost fifty thousand six hundred one dollars. Jalopnik pointed out that this is more than the average price of a new car in America, which Kelley Blue Book put at fifty thousand five hundred sixty-two dollars in September twenty twenty-six. The carbon trim cost more than a whole normal car.
scenes.caption: CARBON TRIM > AVERAGE NEW CAR

scenes.text: What is it like to live with? Kelley Blue Book lists the Revuelto at ten miles per gallon in the city, seventeen on the highway, and twelve combined, on premium fuel, with a twenty-two point five gallon tank. That is why the Jalopnik test car carried a gas guzzler tax of four thousand five hundred dollars, even though it is a plug-in hybrid.
scenes.caption: 12 MPG COMBINED

scenes.text: Here is the twist. A plug-in hybrid with a gas guzzler tax sounds like a contradiction. But it makes sense once you know the secret of the battery. The pack is small and built for performance, not for long electric driving. So on the official tests, the V12 still does most of the work, and the fuel economy looks like a V12 supercar.
scenes.caption: A HYBRID WITH A GUZZLER TAX

scenes.text: Charging is simple. Kelley Blue Book lists a charge time of about two hours on a two hundred forty volt outlet. Many owners may never plug it in at all, because the V12 can refill the battery while driving. The car does not need a charging habit to deliver its full power.
scenes.caption: 2 HOURS ON 240V

scenes.text: And the warranty is three years with unlimited miles, according to Kelley Blue Book. Insurance estimates are surprisingly modest on paper. MoneyGeek, in August twenty twenty-six, estimated full coverage for a Revuelto at about five hundred thirty-nine dollars a month for a forty-year-old driver with a clean record. Specialist policies can be very different, and we look at the full cost in another video.
scenes.caption: ABOUT $539 A MONTH TO INSURE

scenes.text: Inside, the Revuelto has three screens, a twelve point three inch driver display, an eight point four inch vertical central screen, and a nine point one inch passenger screen, which Car and Driver said was a first for Lamborghini. The start button still hides under a red flap, like the switch of a fighter jet, carried over from the Aventador.
scenes.caption: 3 SCREENS AND A RED FLAP

scenes.text: Lamborghini also turned the Revuelto into a canvas. Its Ad Personam department built one-off cars called Opera Unica, with hand-painted liveries and custom interiors, including one inspired by the Taurus constellation and one inspired by Sardinia. There was even a collaboration with Ducati, with a matching Panigale V4 motorcycle and a Revuelto in a two-tone livery.
scenes.caption: OPERA UNICA

scenes.text: And in twenty twenty-six, Lamborghini created Revuelto Italia editions. Wikipedia lists one for the Winter Olympics, revealed on the sixth of February twenty twenty-six in white, and one for the anniversary of the unification of Italy, on the seventeenth of March twenty twenty-six, in blue. The car became part of national celebrations.
scenes.caption: REVUELTO ITALIA, 2026

scenes.text: So let's recap the two secrets. Number one, the gearbox is sideways. It sits behind the engine, across the car, to lower the center of gravity, make room for a working diffuser, and carry an electric motor on top. It also replaced the Aventador's harsh single-clutch gearbox with a smooth eight-speed dual-clutch.
scenes.caption: 1. THE GEARBOX IS SIDEWAYS

scenes.text: Number two, the battery is a spine. A small three point eight kilowatt hour pack runs through the central tunnel, between the seats, where the gearbox used to be. It can refill in minutes, it powers two front motors, and it makes the car faster without making it quiet.
scenes.caption: 2. THE BATTERY IS A SPINE

scenes.text: Put those two secrets together and you understand the Revuelto. Lamborghini did not hybridize the V12 to save it from the future. It moved the gearbox and the battery to build a better V12 supercar, and Top Gear's track verdict suggests it worked.
scenes.caption: A BETTER V12 SUPERCAR

scenes.text: In the other videos of this Revuelto series, we compare it with its biggest rival, the Ferrari twelve Cilindri, we break down what it really costs to own one, and we tell the story of why Lamborghini built it the way it did. Tell us in the comments which secret surprised you more.
scenes.caption: 3 MORE ANGLES
